source.title: Scaling Instruction-Finetuned Language Models
source.authors: Hyung Won Chung; Le Hou; S. Longpre; Barret Zoph; Yi Tay; W. Fedus; Eric Li; Xue-Zhi Wang; Mostafa Dehghani; Siddhartha Brahma; Albert Webson; S. Gu; Zhuyun Dai; M. record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures downstream benchmark performance across model sizes, using accuracy rather than held-out pretraining loss. This tests the downstream-performance version of the claim, but not the original loss-scaling measurement.
record.gate_note: The paper reports downstream benchmark results, not held-out pretraining cross-entropy. Its training-compute figures are costs of instruction finetuning, not a fixed-compute sweep or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. Rows below record normalized-average downstream benchmark scores across model sizes; other benchmark metrics and instruction-finetuning ablations do not measure the scaling relationship named in V6.
record.test_reason: The study reports downstream few-shot benchmark scores across model sizes (T5 80M–11B, PaLM 8B–540B), with and without instruction finetuning. This bears on V6 (downstream improves with scale) in an instruction-finetuned setting. It fits no predictive law and does not relate downstream scores to pretraining loss. No pretraining-loss, extrapolation, allocation or shape analysis is reported, so V1–V5 and V7 are untested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that instruction finetuning improves held-out performance across model families, sizes and objectives, and that performance rises with both model size and number of finetuning tasks. Their scaling curves suggest further gains from larger models and, incrementally, from more tasks. They also say the Flan margin over unfinetuned models does not seem to shrink with scale. They make no claims about pretraining-loss power laws.
record.recipe_differences: The study sweeps model sizes and evaluates downstream few-shot benchmark accuracy after instruction finetuning; it does not fit held-out pretraining-loss scaling laws or sweep training tokens and compute.
record.method_sensitivity: Model family, parameter count, pretraining objective, and instruction-finetuning status differ across evaluated systems; results are downstream normalized-average scores.

fits_no_version.finding: Instruction-finetuning gains grow with the number of finetuning tasks, with diminishing returns after 282 tasks (Table 3, Fig. 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream gains from instruction finetuning scale with task count, with diminishing returns.

fits_no_version.finding: UL2R continued pretraining (about 0.1% extra compute) improves the downstream score of 540B PaLM, and adds to Flan's gain.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Small objective changes after pretraining shift downstream performance off the parameter-scaling trend.

record.problems: The evidence concerns downstream benchmark accuracy, not held-out pretraining cross-entropy. No power-law fits, extrapolation checks, fixed-compute allocation sweep, or uncertainty intervals are reported. Comparisons across model families also vary in architecture and training objective.
record.rows_left_out: No rows from the reported normalized-average model-size results in Table 5 were left out. Other individual benchmark scores and instruction-finetuning ablations were omitted because they are not separate measurements of the size-dependent aggregate outcome recorded here.

untested.parts: No fitted law or forecast of downstream scores. Downstream performance is not related to pretraining loss. Only 3 PaLM sizes and 5 T5 sizes, with no uncertainty.
No fits or extrapolation from small runs.
No power-law fit for finetuning or other regimes. Instruction-finetuning task-count curves are not loss power laws.

missing.what: Unfinetuned models gain from CoT on BBH only at 62B+, an emergence-like discontinuity in downstream scaling
missing.locator: Appendix A.2; Table 5 BBH Direct vs CoT

missing.what: Zero-shot BBH accuracy across 8B/62B/540B for PaLM and Flan-PaLM, with and without CoT
Winogender accuracy: authors state scale has no clear linear influence for Flan-PaLM, and Flan-T5-XXL beats all Flan-PaLM
Per-benchmark Table 5 columns showing T5 TyDiQA at 0.0 and MGSM about 1% at all sizes
Translation misgendering overall accuracy rises with PaLM size (90/95/97)

record.verdict_notes: Tranche changed from T2 to T3: the size sweep is evaluated in a new setting (instruction finetuning), not a different method aimed at loss scaling. Only 3–5 size points per family and no fits, so 'predictably' is untested. R17/R18 are really token-scaling comparisons; R19/R20 are objective changes and are unlinked.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss measured as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
No power-law fits or predictions from small runs to larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or estimate of compute-optimal parameter and token counts.
Architecture families are evaluated, but there is no controlled fixed-parameter comparison of architecture effects on loss.
The study concerns language-model instruction finetuning and does not test the same power-law form in other modalities or the listed training regimes.
Tests downstream benchmark accuracy across model sizes, but does not relate downstream performance to pretraining loss or fit a predictive law.
No scaling-law exponents, compute-optimal split, fitting-choice sensitivity, or curve-bending analysis is reported.
